chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abbas al-Naqid who said:

What was in my possession dispersed, and my business associates left me. So I complained of that to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), and he said to me: Combine the two prayers, the Dhuhr and the Asr — you will see what you love.

key_terms.الصلاتين الظهر والعصر: The two midday prayers (Dhuhr and Asr), which according to Shia jurisprudence may be combined
key_terms.تفرّق: Dispersed, scattered — used for both belongings and people departing
key_terms.حرفاء: Business associates or skilled trade partners; plural of harifi, one engaged in the same craft or trade

ai.seo_question: Does combining the Dhuhr and Asr prayers help with financial hardship according to Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: Abbas al-Naqid, a money-changer and companion of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (AS), reports that he had suffered financial losses and the departure of his business partners. When he brought this complaint to the Imam, he was advised to combine the Dhuhr and Asr prayers, with the promise that doing so would bring relief. This hadith is found in the chapter on combining the two prayers and indicates a practical spiritual remedy recommended by the Imam for hardship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Abbas Al Naqid who said,

‘There has separated from me what was in my hands (belongings) and there have separated my business associates from me. So I complained of that to Abu Muhammadasws, and heasws said to me: ‘Gather between the two Salāts, Al-Zohr and Al-Asr. You shall see what you love’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from ‘Abbas al-Naqid who has said the following:

“My belongings and associates were scattered and I complained about it before abu Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said, ‘Perform al-Dhuhr and al-‘Asr Salah (prayer) soon after the other; you will see whatever you love.’”
